clue.text: Persuade in what children know is true

definitions.meaning: to persuade someone is to bring them to accept a thing as real
the pretend world of games, which children treat as real while playing

explanation.surface: Coaxing someone into accepting what every child is sure of.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a verb phrase for convincing and a noun for the fantasy of play-acting.

clue.text: First Scotsman? The original car, perhaps

definitions.note: the clue means the road surface that came before tarmac

parts.note: Mac is the familiar crossword name for a Scotsman, from the surname prefix
Adam was the first man in the Bible

explanation.surface: A query about the earliest Scot, then a guess at the first ever motor car.
explanation.walkthrough: The road surface is named after the Scottish engineer John McAdam; tarmac (tar macadam) came later, so this is the original road material.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam was the crushed-stone road surface laid before bitumen was added to bind it.

clue.text: Tuneful mother who had a doorstep

definitions.text: Tuneful mother who had a doorstep

parts.words: Tuneful mother who had a doorstep
parts.note: points to the old music-hall song about a mother's front step in a poor street

explanation.surface: A singing mum who owned a front step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On Mother Kelly's Doorstep' is a British music-hall song of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title names its mother figure by this surname.

definitions.meaning: an artillery shell or bomb that detonates

explanation.definitionFit: The word means literally a shell full of explosive and figuratively a stunning revelation.

parts.note: the resting place of the snake from the other clue, a wild creature's den

explanation.surface: Where the snake hangs out.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is the hiding place of a wild animal such as a snake.

parts.note: a salute toward the political left, read as a parade-ground command to turn the head

explanation.surface: A greeting given by comrades on the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: On parade the command makes soldiers turn their heads to the left, as a salute to a reviewing officer; 'Socialist' plays on left-wing politics.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill order makes marching troops salute by looking to the left side.

parts.note: skaters trace a looping number shape on the rink

explanation.surface: A shape a skater carves into the rink.
explanation.definitionFit: Figure skaters trace a figure of this number on the ice, and it is a numeral.

clue.text: A soft sort of pearl outfit

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: a sort of pearl is the word pearl reshaped, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A gentle kind of pearl outfit, as in a soft pearl-coloured ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges PEARL into PAREL, after A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn together is both an outfit and attire.

definitions.meaning: the act of steering a vessel
the cheapest passenger quarters deep in a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the steering of a vessel and its lowest-class accommodation.

definitions.meaning: the clue's adjective stands for a herbaceous plant, the aquilegia
the sweetheart of Harlequin in traditional pantomime

explanation.surface: A leafy sweetheart in a Christmas show.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the flower also called aquilegia and Harlequin's lover in the harlequinade.

definitions.meaning: to stand up or leave one's bed
an informal word for a costume or set of clothes

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a verb for rising from bed and a noun for a costume.

parts.note: describes someone only partly abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone who more or less avoids drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is dry abstains from alcohol, so being somewhat so is half-hearted abstinence.

clue.text: Especially when offered poor ale in the apartment!

definitions.text: Especially when offered poor ale in the apartment!

parts.words: Especially when offered poor ale in the apartment!
parts.note: lifeless ale is one reading, and drink kept in a home apartment is the other

explanation.surface: Complaining about stale beer served at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: ale gone stale is lifeless, and beer kept in a home (a British flat) is literally the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale that has lost its fizz is described as lifeless, and an apartment is a flat.

indicators.note: the word sounds tells us to swap in a word pronounced the same way

parts.note: hired muscle are toughs, heavies paid for strength

explanation.surface: A shellfish that sounds chewy.
explanation.definitionFit: This bivalve is a common edible shellfish.

clue.text: Doesn't sound like a nimble fielder

definitions.text: Doesn't sound like a nimble fielder

parts.words: Doesn't sound like a nimble fielder
parts.note: a cricket position whose name suggests a stumpy limb

explanation.surface: A slow-sounding cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket this is a close fielding position on the leg side near the batsman; its name suggests a stubby limb, hardly nimble.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder placed close in on the leg side is in this position.

definitions.meaning: coming at the very end, behind everyone
nevertheless, in spite of what was expected

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean following every other one, and it is also an idiom meaning nevertheless.

clue.text: Not ensure to be in confidence

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are to be made into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Avoiding a guarantee so as to keep things secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' signals that NOT ENSURE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning between ourselves, said of something told privately.

parts.note: the girl in Uncle Tom's Cabin who said she just grew

explanation.surface: Asking what a famous girl got up to.
explanation.walkthrough: Topsy in Uncle Tom's Cabin says she 'just growed', hence the saying 'grew like Topsy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing larger is to increase in size.

parts.note: a stroke as a medical seizure, which may or may not prove fatal

explanation.surface: A remark about a last strike in a game, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for a cerebral stroke, a seizure that is not always fatal.

indicators.note: telling the words not to be as they are signals their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protesting at being called mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or foolish, literally like a donkey.

clue.text: Arrange a rest in the ship as a cure for it

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is a steamship

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a new order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Booking a relaxing cruise as a cure for tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' turns REST into TRES, which 'in' puts inside SS. 'it' is the definition: rest cures tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest is a cure for tension and anxiety, which is what 'it' points to.

parts.note: the creature in Eden that tempted Eve

explanation.surface: A charmer in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the snake beguiled Eve in the Garden of Eden.

parts.note: to inter is to bury
a war is an armed conflict

explanation.surface: Laying a dispute to rest between battles.
explanation.definitionFit: The years between the two World Wars are described by this word.

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards, so it works in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A spinner that goes either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part, as of a helicopter, spins.

clue.text: Fear to make a mistake in the mountain

indicators.note: the error goes inside the hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Being afraid of slipping up on a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme fear or dread.

clue.text: Where the Nibelung maidens were at home

definitions.text: Where the Nibelung maidens were at home

parts.words: Where the Nibelung maidens were at home
parts.note: the river guarded by the ... in Wagner's Ring cycle

explanation.surface: Asking where some legendary maidens lived.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wagner's Ring the maidens guard the gold in this German river.

parts.note: two pairs of horses drawing a coach

explanation.surface: Two pairs hitched to a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Two pairs make this number, as in a coach and horses drawn by that many.

definitions.meaning: the state of a patient after a stroke

explanation.definitionFit: Motionless describes both an idle thing and a patient left immobile after a seizure.

clue.text: Cutting off one's nose would really do it!

definitions.text: Cutting off one's nose would really do it!

parts.words: Cutting off one's nose would really do it!
parts.note: removing the nose stops smells, a joke on removing odour

explanation.surface: A drastic remedy, as in cutting off your nose to spite your face.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as DE-ODOR-ISE; a playful reading is to de-nose, as removing the nose leaves no smell.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove or mask an unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Muslim Cross society for a street of blood

parts.note: blood is red
a crescent is a curved street

explanation.surface: A society named after a bloody street.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Cross counterpart in Muslim countries; a crescent is a curved British street.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanitarian organisation is the equivalent of the Red Cross in Islamic countries.
